1401: from δέω; a slave (literal or figurative, involuntary or voluntary; frequently, therefore in a qualified sense of subjection or subserviency):--bond(-man), servant.
1402: from δοῦλος; to enslave (literally or figuratively):--bring into (be under) bondage, X given, become (make) servant.
1403: from δέχομαι; a reception, i.e. convivial entertainment:--feast.
1404: probably from an alternate form of (to look); a fabulous kind of serpent (perhaps as supposed to fascinate):--dragon.

1406: from δράσσομαι; a drachma or (silver) coin (as handled):--piece (of silver).
1407: from (to pluck); a gathering hook (especially for harvesting):--sickle.
1408: from the alternate of τρέχω; a race, i.e. (figuratively) career:--course.
1409: a feminine diminutive of Drusus (a Roman name); Drusilla, a member of the Herodian family:--Drusilla.

1413: from δύναμαι; a ruler or officer:--of great authority, mighty, potentate.
1414: from δυνατός; to be efficient (figuratively):--be mighty.

1425: from δυσ- and a derivative of νοιέω; difficult of perception:--hard to be understood.
1426: from a compound of δυσ- and φήμη; defamation:--evil report.
1427: from δύο and δέκα; two and ten, i.e. a dozen:--twelve.
1429: from δώδεκα and φυλή; the commonwealth of Israel:--twelve tribes.
1430: from (to build); properly, an edifice, i.e. (specially) a roof:--housetop.
1432: accusative case of δωρεά as adverb; gratuitously (literally or figuratively):--without a cause, freely, for naught, in vain.

1436: apparent imperative of ἐάω; properly, let it be, i.e. (as interjection) aha!:--let alone.
1437: from εἰ and ἄν; a conditional particle; in case that, provided, etc.; often used in connection with other particles to denote indefiniteness or uncertainty:--before, but, except, (and) if, (if) so, (what-, whither-)soever, though, when (-soever), whether (or), to whom, (who-)so(-ever). 1444: from Ἐβέρ; Hebraic or the Jewish language:--Hebrew.
1445: from Ἐβέρ; a Hebræan (i.e. Hebrew) or Jew:--Hebrew.
1446: from Ἐβέρ; the Hebraistic (Hebrew) or Jewish (Chaldee) language:--Hebrew.

1448: from ἐγγύς; to make near, i.e. (reflexively) approach:--approach, be at hand, come (draw) near, be (come, draw) nigh.
1449: from ἐν and γράφω; to "engrave", i.e. inscribe:--write (in).
1450: from ἐν and (a limb); pledged (as if articulated by a member), i.e. a bondsman:--surety.

1457: from ἐγκαίνια; to renew, i.e. inaugurate:--consecrate, dedicate.
1458: from ἐν and καλέω; to call in (as a debt or demand), i.e. bring to account (charge, criminate, etc.):--accuse, call in question, implead, lay to the charge.
1459: from ἐν and καταλείπω; to leave behind in some place, i.e. (in a good sense) let remain over, or (in a bad sense) to desert:--forsake, leave.
1460: from ἐν and κατοικέω; to settle down in a place, i.e. reside:--dwell among.
1461: from ἐν and a derivative of κέντρον; to prick in, i.e. ingraft:--graff in(-to).

1468: from ἐν and κράτος; strong in a thing (masterful), i.e. (figuratively and reflexively) self-controlled (in appetite, etc.):--temperate.
1469: from ἐν and κρίνω; to judge in, i.e. count among:--make of the number.
1470: from ἐν and κρύπτω; to conceal in, i.e. incorporate with:--hid in.

1472: from ἐν and χρίω; to rub in (oil), i.e. besmear:--anoint.

1474: from ἔδαφος; to raze:--lay even with the ground.
1475: from the base of ἑδραῖος; a basis (bottom), i.e. the soil:--ground.

1481: from ἔθνος and ἀρχή; the governor (not king) of a district:--ethnarch.

1489: from εἰ and γέ; if indeed, seeing that, unless, (with negative) otherwise:--if (so be that, yet).
